div.head: EGu Prol.
div.ab: And þis is seo gerædnis eac, þe Ælfred cyng ⁊ Guðrum cyng ⁊ eft Eadward cyng (⁊ Guðrum cyng) gecuran and gecwædon, þa þa Engle ⁊ Dene to friðe ⁊ to freondscipe fullice fengon; ⁊ þa witan eac, þe syððan wæron, oft ⁊ unseldan þæt seolfe geniwodon ⁊ mid gode geiehtan.

This is also the legislation, which King Alfred and King Guthrum, and afterwards King Edward and King Guthrum, enacted and agreed upon, when the English and the Danes unreservedly entered into relations of peace and friendship. The councillors also who have been [in office] since then, frequently and often have re-enacted the same, and added improvements thereto.

And ðis is seo gerædnyss eac, ðe Ælfred cyng ⁊ Guþrum cyng ⁊ eft Eadward cyng (⁊ Guþrum cyng) gecuran and gecwædon, ða ða Engle ⁊ Dene to friðe ⁊ to freondscipe fullice fengon; ⁊ ða witan eac, ðe syððan wæron, oft ⁊ unseldan þæt seolfe geniwodon ⁊ mid gode gehuhtan.
